Where med spa bookings leak.

Demand is rarely the problem. The leaks sit between the ad and the appointment, and between the first visit and the second.

  • The ad sells a first-visit offer and the page is the full menu.

    The client cannot find the offer they tapped on.

  • Direct messages sit unanswered.

    A question sent at 8pm is seen the next afternoon.

  • Price is "book a consult to find out".

    Clients move on to the provider who gave a starting price.

  • Clients are not rebooked.

    A treatment that lasts three or four months is never followed by a reminder.

  • No-shows.

    Consults are booked on impulse and forgotten without a reminder.

Test your own path in five minutes.

Any "no", or a reply that took more than an hour, is where booked appointments are going.

The full five-minute audit
  1. Tap your own ad on a phone. Is the offer on the first screen of the page it opens?
  2. Send your own business a direct message at 8pm asking for a price.
  3. Write down when the reply arrives and whether it gives a number and a time.
  4. Pull a list of clients whose last visit was four to six months ago. Has anyone contacted them?

Questions from med spas.

  • We get most inquiries on Instagram. Does this cover direct messages?

    Yes. Direct messages, website forms, ad lead forms and missed calls are answered from one place, so nobody waits because of where they wrote.

  • Can we avoid discounting?

    Yes. The offer can be a free consult, a skin assessment or a package. It needs to be clear, not cheap.

  • Do replies give medical advice?

    No. Replies cover prices, availability and booking. Anything clinical is left for the consult with your provider.

  • How do you bring past clients back?

    We segment your client list by treatment and last visit, then send a short reminder with times to book when they are due.
